  • Nicolò Tresoldi silences the San Siro 🤫Club Brugge stun Inter 🥶 pic.twitter.com/D8TIEn6b9C.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is a latest talent in Europe who will make his name in the near future, and that's Nicolò Tresoldi. The 22-year-old is right now playing for Club Brugge and on October 13 scored three goals at San Siro against Inter, showing the world he's ready for the next step in his career. 2027 will be a pivotal year in Tresoldi's career, not only because he could be on the verge of a move to a bigger European club, but also because he may have to make a definitive decision about his international future. With Germany, Italy and Argentina all potentially in the picture, choosing which national team to represent could prove just as significant as his next club move.

Industry observers note that when Tresoldi, the son of a former Serie A player, scored the hat-trick against Inter at San Siro, all the headlines were about his childhood and his love for AC Milan, the Nerazzurri's biggest rival, who, according to reports, are also in talks to potentially sign him in the future. But just how special is Tresoldi, and which European giants could be in the running to sign him in 2027?

Nicolò Tresoldi silences the San Siro 🤫Club Brugge stun Inter 🥶 pic.twitter.com/D8TIEn6b9C.

It has been revealed that tresoldi was born in Cagliari, Sardinia, in 2004, during the summer months when his family would regularly spend time on the island. His connection to Sardinia stemmed from his maternal grandfather, who worked there as a golf instructor. Thanks to this family connection, they had a house on the island and would spend part of their summers there, but because of his mother's job, he moved with his family to Hannover in 2017, when he was 13.

Tresoldi, who until then had played tennis more regularly, decided to start his soccer career in the Hannover academy, where he debuted with the second team before making his first-team debut in 2022. He immediately drew interest from multiple European clubs, and in the summer of 2025 he joined Club Brugge in Belgium, his first major move as a professional soccer player. In his first season at the club, he scored 23 goals in 58 games, including four in the Champions League's league phase, and he has started his second season even better, with 15 goals in all competitions so far, including that unforgettable hat-trick against Inter in Milan.

It has been revealed that next year will also be the year he makes a final decision about which national team he wants to represent. Tresoldi is eligible for Germany, Italy and Argentina. In 2023, he decided to join the German U21 team, and he now intends to see out the entire cycle through the 2027 U21 European Championship, which will take place in the summer. Until then, he won't make a final decision, but both Italy coach Roberto Mancini and Germany coach Jürgen Klopp have expressed interest in calling him up.

Speaking on the topic and about Tresoldi's future, Klopp said: "It doesn't mean that he has made a decision against Germany or Italy. We don't want to put any pressure on the players. It's a sensitive matter, and we will respect whatever decision he makes, without rushing him." Mancini, on the other hand, seemed more optimistic about him choosing Italy: "I've spoken to Tresoldi myself. He needs to feel that he wants to represent our national team. Given that he was born in Italy and has an Italian father, I believe there is a possibility. We hope he makes the right choice; he knows how much he would mean to us." Argentina can also hope to call him up, as his mother is from there, and he could be included in Lionel Scaloni's squad. However, Italy and Germany are his most likely choices.

It has been revealed that before that, he will also be the subject of transfer rumors starting in the early months of the latest year, as many top European clubs are looking for a new striker. AC Milan have to be on that list, as the Rossoneri will likely sign a new striker to play alongside Gonçalo Ramos, even though Club Brugge reportedly value him at around $50 million. At the same time, we need to monitor what Bayern Munich do in the January transfer window, as Harry Kane's injury might force the German side to change strategy in the short term. For sure, 2027 will be the year of Tresoldi, as he now focuses his attention on two moves that will shape his future.

While the Spaniard is unlikely to be out for a prolonged period, it is a headache Mikel Arteta could have done without as he prepares for tonight's Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund and Sunday's visit of Manchester City in the league.

Kepa Arrizabalaga will likely step in as the Gunners attempt to take a big step towards securing a top-eight place, having already gained 10 points from their opening four league phase matches.

It has been revealed that bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are the only other injury absentees for a game in which Arsenal could equal Liverpool's English record of 13 successive home victories in the league phase/group stage. You would be a brave person to bet against them, with Arteta's side winning all six of their matches at the Emirates Stadium this season.

SEE ALSO How to watch Champions League 2026/27.

Dortmund arrive in North London with a spring in their step after returning to the top of the Bundesliga last weekend, courtesy of their 1-0 win at Borussia Mönchengladbach and Bayern Munich's 1-1 draw with Cologne.

Niko Kovac's side will be aiming to go one better than Bayern again tonight, after the Bavarians were held to a 2-2 draw by Arsenal last month.

Dortmund are unbeaten in their last eight matches, but their most recent defeat came in this competition, when they lost 1-0 to Bodø/Glimt. They have since beaten Sabah and Real Betis in the league phase to get back on track.

Kovac is sweating on the fitness of former Aston Villa and Chelsea midfielder Carney Chukwuemeka and top goalscorer Serhou Guirassy, but will definitely be without Emre Can, Samuele Inacio, Justin Lerma, Giannis Konstantelias and Mussa Kaba due to injury.

The Gunners' excellent home record and miserly defence points to a tight home win.
